jonny-desktop.task: meristem: static-region mask for poses - action frames move 53-91 percent of pixels because a whole-figure translate cancels the foot anchor
jonny-desktop.note: DONE + PUSHED. meristem @ d81195c on main; vanguard @ 412aadd on regions/side-areas. Added a STATIC-REGION MASK to the pose system, prompted by the user's sprite-resources doc. Root cause named: lean anchored the feet and a whole-figure shift in the same recipe moved them anyway, so an action frame changed 53-91 percent of its pixels between adjacent frames and the sprite slid rather than pivoting - the opposite of style guide 5.1 'feet must plant rather than slide'. BAND_HOLD declares how many bottom rows a band may not move; hold_static restores them from the idle after transforms; translation dropped from the action recipes since lean carries the motion and a whole-figure translate only moves the planted rows for the mask to undo. Death holds nothing, the figure is meant to leave the ground. Sword churn 85->72, 82->68, 73->55 percent. 96 tests plus two new ones pinning the planted rows and a churn ceiling. Vanguard rebaked (92 sheets), 1100 resources load. IMPORTANT CORRECTION recorded in DECISIONS.md rather than dropped: I reached for this as a fix for 'pixel dancing' and that diagnosis was WRONG. Churn measures the MAGNITUDE of change, not its coherence - a shear moves the whole torso together and a wind-up into a strike is supposed to be a large change, so 55-72 percent is fine. Dancing is unrelated pixels flickering because frames were drawn independently, which transform-derived poses CANNOT do since every frame comes from one idle. The band where dancing could occur is walk, which uses separately-drawn archetype frames, and that measures 3-31 percent. The mask still earns its place, for the reason the style guide gives rather than the one I reached for. NEW FINDING from the meristem reference sheets (docs/reference/vanguard-bestiary.png), which label each creature's ARCHETYPE: 19 of 43 creatures are 'humanoid' and they are near-identical body-with-palette-swap - including granite_golem, lattice_sentinel and crystallized_stillkeeper, which should not be people-shaped at all. That is the same silhouette problem found earlier on three bosses, but at ~19 sprites rather than 3, and it is the largest remaining art issue. Fixing it means new archetypes (golem/construct) in Meristem, not a recolour.
